definition: OpenLogos is an open source program that translates from English and German into French, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese.
details: It accepts various document formats and maintains the format of the original document in translation. OpenLogos does not claim to replace human translators; rather, it aims to enhance the human translator's work environment. The OpenLogos program is based on the Logos Machine Translation System, one of the earliest commercial machine translation programs. The original program was developed by Logos Corporation in the United States, with additional development teams in Germany and Italy.

explainer.lead: OpenLogos is an open-source machine translation program translating English and German into French, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese. It descends from one of the earliest commercial MT systems and is positioned as a translator aid rather than a replacement.

tiers.eli5: It is a free translation tool that turns English or German documents into Romance languages while keeping the document looking the same.
tiers.practitioner: Users feed documents in common formats and get translated versions that preserve the original layout, then edit the output. It is meant to assist human translators, so outputs are not assumed to be publish-ready.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a rule-based translation program derived from the Logos Machine Translation System; no accuracy guarantees are stated for its output.

explainer.example: A German report is submitted in its original format and returned in French with the formatting preserved for a translator to review.
